title: solidity detail string labels the normalized score (1 − solidity) as "solidity:", inverting the metric for direction="below"
benefit_rationale: The numeric score the benchmark folds into overall is correct — the solidity primitive returns a sensible 0..1 pass-score, so the weighted overall is NOT corrupted. The harm is purely diagnostic/agent-facing: the detail line is the human/agent-readable explanation, and for the default and documented config (direction="below") it prints "solidity: 0.6000" when the geometric solidity is actually 0.40. An agent reading its own evaluate_design output to decide whether to reshape the mesa will misread a passing concave mesa as failing (and vice-versa) and may act counterproductively (e.g. making the mesa MORE convex to "raise solidity", which lowers the actual score). Since e2e_design is explicitly agent-in-the-loop (the SKILL tells the agent to read check details and iterate), a self-inverting diagnostic can drag iteration the wrong way and waste turns. Fixing it plausibly improves stability on shape-targeted task-types, though it will not move the raw metric on a one-shot run. Low-to-moderate value: cosmetic relative to the false-zero / arm_material_class fixes, but cheap and strictly positive.
current_behavior: _prim_solidity (tools/evaluate_worker.py:634-648) returns a bare float. For direction=="below" (the default, line 644, and the canonical Hall-bar example in skills/nanodevice_e2e_design/SKILL.md:216) it returns max(0,min(1, 1.0 - solidity)) when solidity<threshold else 0.0 (line 646). Because the return is a float (not a dict carrying its own "detail"), the check loop falls through to the generic formatter at tools/evaluate_worker.py:1086: detail = "{}: {:.4f}".format(name, score). The result is a detail string "solidity: 0.6000" whose number is actually (1 − raw_solidity), not the geometric solidity. Example: a mesa with raw solidity 0.40 (passing, concave, score 0.60) prints "solidity: 0.6000" and reads as if solidity were 0.60 (would-be fail). For direction=="above" (line 648) the returned score equals raw solidity, so the label is coincidentally correct there.
evidence: tools/evaluate_worker.py:634-648 — _prim_solidity returns a bare float; line 642 computes raw solidity = comp.area/hull.area; line 646 returns 1.0 - solidity for direction='below' (default per line 644)
tools/evaluate_worker.py:1083-1086 — detail built generically: when raw is not a dict-with-'detail', detail = "{}: {:.4f}".format(name, score) -> "solidity: <1-solidity>"
skills/nanodevice_e2e_design/SKILL.md:216 — documented example uses direction='below', threshold=0.5, i.e. the inverted case ships as the recommended config
tools/evaluate_worker.py:644 — direction = args.get('direction', 'below') confirms 'below' is the default
git diff HEAD -- tools/evaluate_worker.py shows no uncommitted changes; working tree == committed; issue is NOT fixed in current tree
recommended_fix: Make _prim_solidity return a dict carrying its own self-describing detail instead of relying on the generic formatter. Compute raw solidity once, then return e.g. {"score": <normalized 0..1>, "detail": "solidity raw={:.4f} threshold={:.2f} direction={} -> score={:.4f}".format(raw_solidity, threshold, direction, score), "extra": {"raw_solidity": raw_solidity, "threshold": threshold, "direction": direction}}. This echoes the true geometric solidity AND the verdict/normalized score separately, eliminating the inversion. The check loop already supports dict returns (tools/evaluate_worker.py:1077-1084 reads score/detail/extra), so no loop change is needed and the weighted overall is unchanged. Residual hardening: adjacency/spacing detail strings would also benefit from echoing the raw fraction, but only solidity actually inverts.
impact: low — affects only the human/agent-readable detail field of the solidity check; does not change score, weight, or overall. Relevant to e2e_design / nanodevice DRC task-types that include a shape (solidity) check, primarily Hall-bar-style devices with a concave mesa goal. No effect on routing-connectivity or flake-detect IoU benchmarks.
risk: Very low. Switching _prim_solidity to a dict return is additive: the check loop (lines 1077-1084) already handles dict returns, score clamping is unchanged, and the weighted overall is computed from "score" which keeps the same value. Only risk is a test that string-matches the OLD detail format "solidity: 0.xxxx" exactly — none exists (no test asserts on the solidity detail string), so regression risk is effectively nil.
test_quality_concern: WEAK coverage for this specific bug. test_solidity_below (test_phase1_worker.py:318-329) only asserts result['checks'][0]['score'] > 0.0 — it never inspects the detail string, so it cannot detect the label/number inversion. The default-config test (line 213) is looser still. The only structural detail test (line 727) just asserts the key 'detail' EXISTS in every check, not its content/correctness. No test anywhere asserts the solidity detail echoes the raw geometric solidity or distinguishes raw from normalized score, so the bug is fully invisible to the current suite. A proper regression test should build a mesa with a known raw solidity (e.g. 0.40 via a controlled hull/area ratio), run with direction='below', and assert the detail reports the RAW solidity (0.40), not 1-solidity (0.60) — asserting behavior, not a hardcoded string literal.

title: auto_route grids the entire cell bbox, not the pin sub-region — OOM/timeout when pads are on a far perimeter
current_behavior: route_worker.py builds the routing cost grid over the ENTIRE cell.bbox() plus a fixed margin (lines 672-676), then rasterizes ncols×nrows over that full span (rasterize_region_kdb, 130-135) and runs MCP_Geometric Dijkstra over the whole array once per net (227-228). When pads sit on a far perimeter the grid spans the full chip; with fine map_resolution (or auto_map_resolution derived from small contacts) the cell count explodes (e.g. 2mm span @ 0.2um = 100M cells, ~1.2GB cost grid) → numpy OOM-kill (exit -9/137) or >600s timeout. There is no routing_bbox param, no two-window inner-fine/outer-coarse mode, and no grid-cell-count guard — only a wall-clock timeout clamped to [10,600]s.
benefit_rationale: High value. The benchmark scores routing connectivity and DRC/metric checks via evaluate_design; a subprocess that exits -9/137 or times out yields ZERO routed pairs and a hard tool failure — the worst outcome for any fixture whose pads are on a perimeter or whose contacts are small enough to trigger fine auto resolution (reported 10/36 fixtures). Cropping the grid to the union of pin bboxes + margin is a pure performance/stability fix with no change to routing semantics on layouts that already fit, so it converts crashed runs into routed runs without risking regressions on passing fixtures, and makes auto_map_resolution safe on small-contact layouts.

tools/route_worker.py:403-414 — auto_map_resolution derives map_res from min pin edge (/3, clamped [0.2,5.0]) but still grids the full bbox, so small contacts make the full-span grid FINER, worsening the blow-up
tools/route_worker.py: grep for routing_bbox|route_bbox|two.window|MAX_|grid cap|n_cells returns nothing — no crop param, no cap, no guard
plugin/klayoutclaw_server.lym:486-519 — auto_route schema exposes map_resolution, auto_map_resolution, timeout(10-600) only; no routing_bbox param
plugin/klayoutclaw_server.lym:1079-1080 — TimeoutExpired only advises raising map_resolution/timeout; no bbox mitigation

recommended_fix: In route_worker.py replace the cell-bbox window (672-676) with a pin-aware window: union all pin-A/pin-B bboxes (extract_pin_bboxes already exists at line 92), include obstacle/keepout shapes intersecting that span, inflate by max(obs_safe_dbu, resolution_dbu*10, freeze_margin_dbu) plus detour slack (~0.25× pin-span diagonal so Dijkstra has room), and clamp to cell.bbox() so it can only shrink. Add a hard grid-cell-count guard before allocation: if ncols*nrows exceeds a cap (e.g. 25M) auto-coarsen map_res to fit or return a structured error advising routing_bbox/coarser resolution instead of letting numpy get OOM-killed. Expose an optional routing_bbox [x1,y1,x2,y2] (um) MCP param in klayoutclaw_server.lym auto_route schema and pass it through to override the auto window. The optional inner-fine/outer-coarse two-window mode is a lower-priority enhancement; the pin-bbox crop + cell-count guard captures nearly all the benefit. All grid coordinate math (dbu_to_grid/grid_to_dbu, rasterize origin, damping origin) already keys off `bbox`, so changing only the bbox definition is self-consistent.
test_quality_concern: No test covers this issue's failure mode — a coverage gap. test_route_worker_override.py uses a tiny 50-102um layout, test_route_worker_rescue.py a roomy 4-contact fan-out, test_phase1_worker_bus.py small bus fixtures. None assert on grid dimensions, cost-array size, a far-perimeter-pad scenario, or any memory/timeout bound, so the bbox-sizing path is wholly untested. Their existing assertions are behaviorally sound for what they target (assignment/override/rescue/bus) — the concern is missing coverage, not a weak/keyword/hardcoded-literal assertion. A proper regression test would build a GDS with pins clustered in one corner and a large empty perimeter, then assert the rasterized grid (reported nrows×ncols or returned grid shape) is bounded by the pin span + margin rather than the full cell bbox — asserting on actual grid shape, not a log string.
impact: high — affects routing-bearing benchmark fixtures whose pads sit on a far perimeter or whose contacts are small enough to trigger fine auto_map_resolution (reported 10/36); failure is a hard subprocess kill (exit -9/137) or 300-600s timeout yielding zero routed pairs, zeroing connectivity/route metrics in evaluate_design for those device-design task-types.
risk: Low-to-medium. Cropping to union(pin bboxes)+margin clamped to cell.bbox() preserves identical routing on layouts that already fit (the window only shrinks where the old one was wastefully large). Main risk: making the window too tight for layouts that must detour around obstacles far from the straight pin span — mitigate by including obstacle shapes in the span and adding generous detour slack, plus clamping to cell.bbox() as the upper bound. The cell-count guard may auto-coarsen borderline-large layouts, but that is strictly better than an OOM kill. Gate with the corner-clustered-pins regression test and re-run override/rescue/bus tests to confirm unchanged paths.

title: route_crossings net-aware primitive (per-route overlap vs arbitrary obstacle layers, grouped by net)
current_behavior: No route_crossings primitive exists. contact_isolation checks route-vs-route crossings only and is NOT net-aware (reports raw [i,j,area] pairs after a junction filter, no electrical-net grouping). route_material_compat checks route-vs-flake-material only, hardcoded to graphene/graphite, not arbitrary obstacle layers and not net-grouped. route_inspect reports per-route metadata + route-vs-route crossings on the SAME route_layer, with no obstacle-layer parameter and no net grouping. component_overlap gives only AGGREGATE (not per-route) overlap of a component vs an arbitrary region. Net identity (net_id) lives only in route_worker.py for pathfinding and is never propagated to evaluation/inspection output.

benefit_rationale: The official benchmark scorer composite_evaluator.py:261-281 (_check_contact_isolation, weight 0.15) counts EVERY route-pair intersection > 1.0 um2 as a crossing with ZERO net-awareness and no same-net exclusion; the full 6-metric scorer (lines 49-56) has no obstacle-layer-crossing metric and no net metric at all. A net-aware route_crossings primitive in the agent tool therefore cannot directly move the benchmark number — it is a self-check/diagnostic aid only. Worse, the requested same-net-touches-not-flagged leniency would DIVERGE from how the scorer actually counts shorts (it does not forgive same-net overlap), so optimizing against a net-lenient self-check could let layouts self-validate as clean while still losing the strict contact_isolation points. The two short-types that actually matter (route-route shorts, route-vs-opposing-flake shorts) are already covered by contact_isolation + route_material_compat, and route_inspect already exposes per-route crossing geometry with route_id alignment. The marginal want (per-route overlap vs arbitrary obstacle layers) is reachable today by adding the obstacle as a route_component / via component_overlap. Low-value wanted feature relative to effort.
recommended_fix: Do NOT add net-aware same-net leniency — it contradicts the official scorer. If hardening is wanted, take the lowest-cost scorer-aligned path: generalize EXISTING per-route diagnostics rather than introduce a net concept. (a) Add an optional obstacle_component arg to _prim_contact_isolation (evaluate_worker.py:288) so it also reports per-route overlap of each route vs an arbitrary layer_map key, returning [route_id, obstacle_idx, area_um2]; or (b) extend route_inspect (klayoutclaw_server.lym:1277) with an optional obstacle_layers param adding per-route obstacle_overlaps=[{route_id, layer, area_um2}]. Keep scoring strict (no same-net forgiveness) to stay consistent with composite_evaluator._check_contact_isolation. Defer net grouping until the official scorer adds a net concept — the agent has no net-id propagation from route_worker into committed GDS today.
impact: low — touches routing/contact_isolation on device-design task-types (e2e_device_design, hallbar/AH/ML benchmark families) only indirectly via self-diagnosis quality; the official scorer is net-agnostic and unaffected by adding this tool, so no direct score lift on any dataset.
risk: Low-to-medium if implemented as a NEW optional arg on existing primitives (additive, default off → no behavior change for current callers). Medium-to-high if a net-lenient route_crossings is added and agents trust it: layouts could self-validate clean while the strict official scorer still flags same-net overlaps as shorts, a silent benchmark regression. Main risk is conceptual misalignment with the scorer, not code fragility.
test_quality_concern: Mixed. STRONG: test_evaluate_worker_overfit.py:522-552 builds a real crossing GDS and asserts both that score drops AND that crossing_pairs is populated with [i,j,area] tuples (behavioral, not keyword-match); test_phase1_worker.py:595-651 (test_matches_official_scorer) re-runs composite_evaluator._check_route_material_compat on the same layouts and compares — a genuine cross-check against ground truth. WEAK: test_phase1_worker.py:275-286 (test_contact_isolation) asserts only score == 1.0 on a clean fixture — a trivially-passable happy-path assertion that would not catch a primitive that always returns 1.0; the real negative (crossing-present) case lives only in the overfit test, not beside it. For the issue itself there are NO tests for route-vs-arbitrary-obstacle-layer overlap or net grouping (feature does not exist), so nothing guards against a future net-lenient implementation diverging from the strict official scorer.

title: Read-only region-algebra / boolean-region MCP helper (analyze_regions/measure_region)
benefit_rationale: The boolean algebra itself (union/intersection/difference + per-region area/bbox/centroid) is already fully implemented and well-tested, so the marginal benchmark lift is moderate, not large. The real value of a standalone read-only tool is ergonomic/stability: today the agent must construct a full evaluate_design check spec (layer_map + weighted checks) just to MEASURE the graphene-graphite overlap during the ANALYZE phase, which is exactly the mandatory frame-guard step (skills/nanodevice_e2e_design/SKILL.md:124). Agents needing this measurement fall back to execute_script + hand-rolled pya.Region code — the very pattern the schema text at klayoutclaw_server.lym:550 says material_overlap_report exists to replace. A lightweight read-only helper would remove a class of agent-authored scratch-layer/Region bugs and make the mandatory frame-guard cheaper to satisfy, plausibly improving stability and material-containment checks. Adding solidity/convex_hull per derived region is low-value (no current check consumes it), so most of the wanted surface is already covered.
current_behavior: Region boolean algebra and per-region geometry readout exist ONLY as the material_overlap_report primitive inside evaluate_design (tools/evaluate_worker.py:731-812). It returns score=1.0 always plus a 'report' side-data dict (promoted onto the check at main() line 1113-1115) keyed by '<name>_only' (material minus union of others = subtraction, lines 786-795) and '<a>_and_<b>...' (pairwise + higher-order intersection, lines 797-805). Per region it reports area_um2, bbox_um, centroid_um, num_polygons (_summarize, lines 767-783). General union/intersection/difference over arbitrary layer_map keys is available via _resolve_region (lines 163-192, region_op in {union,intersection,difference}) and is consumed by component_overlap/containment/bulk_containment/arm_material_class. There is NO standalone analyze_regions or measure_region MCP tool (confirmed zero matches repo-wide; plugin exposes 14 tools, none read-only-region). The report does NOT include solidity or convex-hull per region; solidity exists only as a separate single-component scoring primitive (_prim_solidity, lines 634-648) that returns a clamped score, not a measurement, and convex_hull is computed only internally there (line 639).
recommended_fix: Two-tier. (1) Minimal, low-risk: extend _summarize (tools/evaluate_worker.py:767-783) to also emit 'solidity' (region.area / region.convex_hull.area, guarded for empty/zero hull as in _prim_solidity:640) and optionally 'convex_hull_area_um2'. Closes the per-region solidity/convex-hull gap inside the existing report with no new tool surface. (2) The actual ask: add a thin read-only MCP tool 'analyze_regions' in plugin/klayoutclaw_server.lym (alongside _tool_evaluate_design ~line 1697) accepting layer_map + a list of region expressions ({name, region, region_op}) and returning ONLY the _summarize-style measurements without requiring weights or a scoring contract. Implement by reusing _resolve_region + _summarize via the same subprocess path (add an 'analyze' mode to evaluate_worker.main, or a sibling function) so the boolean-algebra logic is not duplicated. Do NOT special-case L11-L13 — keep it layer_map-driven (SKILL.md:124 forbids hard-coding L11/L13). Also strengthen the weak doc-grep test (tests/test_phase4_docs_integration.py:227-234) to assert behavior on a fixture rather than substring presence.

title: auto_route ordered-loop assignment silently produces route-route crossings
benefit_rationale: Route-route crossings directly tank the benchmark via evaluate_design.contact_isolation (crossing_pairs lowers the score below 1.0) and via connectivity caps when the last lead in a dense fan-out fails to route. The bulk of the reported breakage is already addressed: a true cyclic-monotonic DP prevents crossings in the assignment, completed routes freeze as hard obstacles, and the dense-fan-out rescue keeps real path cells (-3.0) hard so a rescued lead can never cut through a prior route. title: connectivity/contact_isolation arg schema undiscoverable; unknown arg keys silently ignored, check silently scores 0.0
benefit_rationale: The benchmark scores evaluate_design via weighted per-check scores; a check that silently returns 0.0 because of a typo'd arg key (e.g. 'tolerence' instead of 'tolerance', or 'contact_compoennt') or an unresolved material-layer value drags the weighted overall down on a design that is actually correct. The reported 8/36 CRITICAL frequency is plausible: agents author the checks dict by hand and a single silent key typo costs the whole check's weight with no feedback to self-correct. Surfacing an explicit error (which excludes the check from the weighted overall, as route_material_compat already does) lets the agent immediately fix the call rather than mis-attributing the 0 to its geometry and futilely re-drawing. A describe_checks/introspection mode further reduces the rate of malformed calls at authoring time. This is a stability/score win, not cosmetic. Caveat: raising on unknown keys must be done carefully — Postel's-law leniency elsewhere (arm_material_class accepts 3 class value forms) shows the codebase intentionally tolerates shape variation, so hardening should target genuinely-unrecognized KEY NAMES and unresolved layer_map VALUES, not legitimate alternate value shapes.
recommended_fix: Three layered changes. (1) Server-side unknown-key rejection in plugin/klayoutclaw_server.lym after the required-args loop (~line 1778): define an _allowed_args table per primitive (union of required + optional keys, e.g. component_overlap:{component,region,region_op}; connectivity:{contact_component,pad_component,route_component,tolerance}; contact_isolation:{component}; etc.), then for each check raise ValueError("checks[i] ('name') has unknown arg 'X'. Allowed: [...]") for any key not in that set. (2) Extend the layer_map-value validation (the _component_keys block, ~line 1781) to also validate the layer_map-referencing VALUES of materials, bulk_region, graphene, graphite, and each str/list-of-str entry of classes, so a typo in those raises the same actionable 'not found in layer_map' error instead of resolving to an empty region and silent 0.0. (3) Add a 'describe_checks' (or 'mode':'describe') path that returns _known_primitives + _required_args + _allowed_args as structured JSON without saving/spawning the subprocess, making each primitive's required/optional args machine-discoverable. Residual hardening: replicate route_material_compat's raise-instead-of-false-zero pattern (worker:427-444) to other primitives whose empty key resolution yields 0.0 via _component_union returning sg.Polygon() (worker:102-110), OR rely on (1)+(2) to catch typos before the subprocess runs (preferred — feedback before computation).
impact: med — affects every benchmark task that calls evaluate_design with hand-authored checks (DRC/metric-scored device-design task-types: hallbar + non-hallbar E2E design, routing connectivity, material-containment). Does NOT affect flake-detect IoU/reward tasks (they don't call evaluate_design). Reported 8/36 frequency concentrated in the device-design benchmark family.
current_behavior: Unknown/misspelled arg KEY names in a check's args dict are silently ignored — the worker reads every optional arg via args.get(key, default), so a typo falls through to the default with no error (tools/evaluate_worker.py:298,407-412,539-542,585-587,629,643-644,661,701,711-714,840,844). benefit_rationale: The benchmark scores routing connectivity (routed_pairs / n) and contact_isolation crossings. The opt-in auto_map_resolution helps map_resolution, but it is OFF by default, so an agent that does not know to flip it (most benchmark runs use plain defaults) still hits the coarse path. Auto-deriving sensible scale-aware defaults (or a device-scale preset) would lift connectivity/crossing scores on the sub-30um task subset without the agent needing tribal knowledge. title: auto_route long-call HTTP fetch fails even on routing success; ping probe does not fix it
benefit_rationale: The benchmark scores routing connectivity (contacts reaching pads) and downstream DRC/metric checks on the routed layout. A "fetch failed" on a route that actually succeeded server-side is a pure false negative: the agent sees an error, may abandon or re-run the route (also slow, can wedge or duplicate geometry), and the connectivity/route_endpoints checks then score 0 even though valid traces exist on disk. Reported CRITICAL at 2/36 — low frequency but each occurrence likely zeroes a whole routed case. Value is bounded: it only bites at fine map_resolution / large fan-outs that exceed the transport's tolerance, so realistic upside is a few cases, not a broad lift.
current_behavior: Server is a single-threaded pya.QTcpServer on the Qt main thread. tools/call for auto_route runs subprocess.run(..., timeout) synchronously (klayoutclaw_server.lym:2420 -> _tool_auto_route -> :1075-1078), blocking the entire Qt event loop; the HTTP response is written only after the tool returns (:2587), over an HTTP/1.0 Connection: close socket (:2459) with no streaming/heartbeat. Client (agent/src/mcp/transport.ts:40-49) does a single fetch with an AbortController and a flat 300_000ms timeout (klayout-client.ts:31), no retry/keepalive/job-id. If the TCP connection drops mid-route, or the route runs past 300s (server timeout clamps to 600s at :976-977, LONGER than the client's 300s cap), the client throws 'fetch failed' even though the route subprocess can finish and write valid traces server-side. The ping method added in 9acac92 (:2376-2383, busy-exempt at :2400-2402) does NOT address this: because subprocess.run blocks the main thread and does not pump the Qt event loop, an incoming ping connection cannot be accepted or serviced while auto_route is in flight, so it provides no heartbeat over the in-flight call.

tests/test_phase0_func.py:48-59 — 'ping' is used only as a connection-availability check, not to test busy-exempt liveness or long-call recovery
recommended_fix: Two complementary, low-risk options. (A) Cheapest correctness fix: raise the client fetch timeout above the server's max subprocess timeout (set DEFAULT_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS >= 600_000 + margin, or derive it from the auto_route 'timeout' arg) so the client never aborts a route the server is still legitimately running — directly removes the 300s-client-vs-600s-server mismatch. (B) For true transport-drop resilience: the auto_route subprocess already writes its result JSON to a deterministic path (output_json, :1084-1089); after a 'fetch failed'/ECONNRESET the client (transport.ts) should do a bounded retry that, instead of re-running the route, first calls a lightweight native tool (read the route layer via execute_script, or a new route_status check) to detect the routes already exist and treat the call as success. Long term, decouple heavy tools from the request thread (job-id submit + poll), but that is a larger refactor of the single-threaded server. Keep the ping probe (genuinely useful for the wedged-bridge case) but stop presenting it as the fix for in-flight long calls. Minimum viable change: bump the client timeout and add a connection-drop retry that confirms server-side success before reporting failure.
impact: med — affects the routing stage of nanodevice_e2e_design / e2e_judge benchmark cases that hit fine map_resolution or large fan-outs (long routes); each false-negative likely zeroes a routed case's connectivity/route_endpoints/DRC score. Low frequency (reported 2/36) but high per-occurrence cost.
test_quality_concern: No test covers this issue at all. The many 'method: ping' usages (test_phase0_func.py:51, test_phase1_mcp.py:30, test_phase4_mcp.py:36, etc.) are weak for THIS purpose: they call ping only as an is-server-reachable check and assert nothing about busy-exempt liveness, in-flight behavior, or long-call recovery — they would pass regardless of whether the long-call bug is fixed. The TS test asserting on the literal 'fetch failed' (agent/tests/test-thinking-only.ts:303) is a string-literal assertion exercising the agent's retry CLASSIFIER, not the KLayout transport, giving false confidence that 'fetch failed' is handled when transport.ts has no retry/job-id path. No test holds a real long auto_route open to reproduce a transport drop or to verify server-side result survives a client abort.
risk: Option A (raise client timeout) is near-zero regression risk — it only lets the client wait longer for calls the server already bounds at 600s; short calls still surface connection errors quickly via the separate short-timeout init/list paths. Option B (drop-retry that confirms server-side success) carries moderate risk: an over-eager retry could mask a genuine failure or, if it re-runs the route, duplicate geometry — it must verify existing routes (not blindly re-run) and be idempotent. The ping mechanism itself is unaffected.

title: Skill SKILL.md files still hardcode `conda run -n instrMCPdev python` (no $PYTHON_PATH indirection); .py scripts only reference it in docstrings; MCP tools already fixed
benefit_rationale: The flake-detect / gdsalign / combine / align pipelines are driven by the agent literally copying the `conda run -n instrMCPdev python ...` commands out of the SKILL.md files and running them via Bash. On any benchmark host where that conda env name is absent (the report's 3/36 = the docker image whose interpreter is /opt/venv/bin/python), every one of those Bash calls exits non-zero, the agent gets no detection output, and the flake-detect IoU/reward score for that run collapses to zero. That is a hard environmental failure, not a quality nuance, so removing the hardcoded env name (or routing it through an env var the harness can set) directly protects the flake-detect score on non-standard hosts. The MCP-tool path (auto_route/evaluate_design) is already hardened via PYTHON_PATH, so routing/DRC scores are not at risk; the residual exposure is the direct-script skills. Effort is low and the change is purely additive (env var with conda fallback), so risk/benefit is clearly positive.
current_behavior: Two distinct invocation paths exist. (1) MCP tools auto_route + evaluate_design spawn the worker subprocess from the .lym and ALREADY honor an interpreter override: `python_path = python_path or os.environ.get('PYTHON_PATH')` (plugin/klayoutclaw_server.lym:1056 and :1851), with a `python_path` tool parameter and a multi-distro conda.sh search (miniforge3/anaconda3/miniconda3) as fallback — this path is fixed. (2) The direct-script skills (flakedetect align/detect/combine, gdsalign) are run by the agent following SKILL.md, which hardcodes literal Bash commands `conda run -n instrMCPdev python <script>` with no env-var indirection; on a host lacking that env those commands fail. The .py scripts themselves never call conda — every `conda run -n instrMCPdev` inside a .py file is in a usage docstring only, so the scripts run fine under any interpreter (e.g. /opt/venv/bin/python footprint.py ...). The uncommitted working-tree edits to footprint.py and graphene.py are memory-bounding refactors and do not touch this issue.

title: Explicit net-label / pin-centroid contact->pad assignment for auto_route
benefit_rationale: The two substantive halves of this WANTED feature already exist and were the high-value ones; the remaining piece (named net labels + "true centroid" snapping) would not move the benchmark. (1) Explicit per-pair contact->pad tuples: ALREADY shipped as pin_pairs_override=[[a_idx,b_idx],...] (route_worker.py:426-451, server schema lines 502-511, committed 4e7d97e). It directly resolved the ml14 blocker that motivated this feedback (agent abandoned auto_route after ~23 calls because ordered-loop pairing couldn't be overridden) — docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-17-benchmark-review-fixes.md:1501-1611. This overlaps almost entirely with issue #6 (same Phase 3 work). (2) Per-pair obstacle tuples: ALREADY shipped as per_pair_obstacle_layers (route_worker.py:318,743-754,810-824; server schema line 501). (3) "Snap endpoints to true centroids rather than shape-iteration order": the only genuinely-missing piece, and low value. Pin markers in this codebase are by construction square pya.Box shapes placed AT the contact center (place_pads.py:97, create_hallbar_unrouted.py:75-78), so the bbox-center used by extract_pin_centers (route_worker.py:85-88) is EXACTLY the true centroid — no centroid error to fix for the benchmark convention. Index-vs-name addressing is usability, not a connectivity/DRC/IoU lever: dry_run already returns pin_a_um/pin_b_um world coords + indices (route_worker.py:716-741) so an agent can map names->indices itself. Connectivity scoring (evaluate_design.connectivity / route_endpoints) is geometric and index-agnostic. Net labels would add text-shape parsing surface (absent everywhere — is_text() at lym:879,1336,1363 only SKIPS text) for no scoring gain.
current_behavior: auto_route assigns contacts->pads three ways: automatic ordered-loop (default, route_worker.py:547-569), auto-cluster bus detection (453-512), and explicit pin_pairs_override by integer index (426-451). bus_pairs supports multi-sink nets (514-545). Endpoints come from extract_pin_centers, returning each pin's bbox center ((left+right)//2,(bottom+top)//2) in shape-iteration order (79-89); for the square Box pin markers the codebase uses, that equals the true centroid. dry_run returns pairs[] with both indices and um coords (716-741). per_pair_obstacle_layers adds obstacles to individual pairs (810-824). There is NO net-name/label support and NO polygon-centroid (vs bbox-center) computation anywhere in route_worker.py or route_inspect.
